comparisons.peer_summary: Unrecognized tax benefits impacting the effective tax rate were $1.3 billion as of 2024 and 2023, with accrued penalties and interest of $298 million; long-term income tax liabilities for these benefits totaled $1.4 billion as of 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and INTC disclose long-term income tax liabilities specifically related to uncertain tax positions, though the magnitude and primary drivers differ significantly. AMD reports $1.4 billion in long-term income tax liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits as of Dec 28, 2024. INTC also identifies 'amounts for uncertain tax positions' as a component of its $1.6 billion long-term income taxes payable, but its primary driver is the $1.6 billion transition tax from Tax Reform payable over eight years. While both companies carry substantial long-term tax liabilities for uncertain positions/transition tax, INTC's liability is heavily influenced by the one-time transition tax from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, whereas AMD's is purely characterized as unrecognized tax benefits without mention of transition tax.

sentences.text: Long-term income taxes payable of $1.6 billion as of December 28, 2024 ($2.6 billion as of December 30, 2023) are primarily composed of the transition tax from Tax Reform, which is payable over eight years beginning in 2018, as well as amounts for uncertain tax positions, reduced by the associated deduction for state taxes and non-US tax credits.

As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had long-term income tax liabilities related to unrecognized tax benefits of $1.4 billion, recorded under Other long-term liabilities in the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheets.

comparisons.peer_topic: Unrecognized Tax Benefits Reconciliation and Amounts
comparisons.peer_summary: The company recognized $144 million, $22 million, and $25 million in interest and penalties during fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively, with total accrued interest and penalties reaching approximately $701 million as of November 3, 2024, primarily due to the VMware acquisition and current year accruals. Approximately $6,544 million and $5,044 million of unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest and penalties would benefit the effective income tax rate if recognized as of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both INTC and AVGO disclose significant unrecognized tax benefits and associated interest/penalties that would benefit the effective tax rate if recognized, indicating similar exposure to uncertain tax positions. As of Nov 3, 2024, AVGO had approximately $6,544 million of unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest/penalties that would benefit the effective tax rate, whereas INTC’s long-term income taxes payable included amounts for uncertain tax positions (part of the $1.6 billion total, distinct from the $1.6 billion transition tax). Both companies accrue interest and penalties related to these positions within the income tax provision, though AVGO reports specific historical accruals ($144 million in 2024) while INTC does not quantify the interest/penalty component of its uncertain tax positions separately in the cited sentence.

sentences.text: Long-term income taxes payable of $1.6 billion as of December 28, 2024 ($2.6 billion as of December 30, 2023) are primarily composed of the transition tax from Tax Reform, which is payable over eight years beginning in 2018, as well as amounts for uncertain tax positions, reduced by the associated deduction for state taxes and non-US tax credits.

As of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, approximately $6,544 million and $5,044 million, respectively, of the unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest and penalties would, if recognized, benefit our effective income tax rate.
